narrative:
The model estimated an 87% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, and that high failure risk is why your application was denied. In practical terms, your profile looked much closer to students who failed than to students who passed, so the admission decision followed that prediction.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You are in decile 1, while accepted students averaged around decile 5.8; this low standing was the largest push toward the failure prediction. The second strongest factor was your part-time status. Accepted students were overwhelmingly full-time, so being part-time also moved your prediction toward failure. The third factor was your first-year class standing: decile 3 compared with an accepted average near decile 6, which again pushed toward failure, though less strongly than your third-year standing. These three factors all pointed in the same direction, so the denial reflects a consistent pattern rather than one isolated weakness.

To move forward, ask admissions for specific feedback, strengthen your academic record where possible, consider retaking the LSAT or improving your GPA, and adjust your study or work plans so you can study full-time or with more support. Reapply only when you can show a stronger recent academic profile and a realistic bar-exam preparation plan.
